Helicobacter pylori bacilli were also identified. The final diagnosis was syphilitic gastritis.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (a, b, c, d). a: Clinical photo from a syphilis case report showing a tongue mass with surrounding white lesion; article title establishes syphilis, and the lesion is the reported manifestation, though the caption does not name a specific syphilitic subtype. b: MRI panel from the same syphilis case shows enhancement of the tongue lesion; signal is not specific, but the case-level diagnosis and captioned anatomic site support inclusion as syphilis-related imaging. c: Ultrasound panel from the syphilis case shows an enlarged cervical lymph node; reactive lymphadenopathy can occur in syphilis, but the caption primarily raises metastasis concern, making attribution less specific. d: Contrast-enhanced CT panel from the syphilis case shows an enlarged cervical lymph node; the caption compares it to SCC metastasis, so specificity for syphilis is limited.

panels.figure_caption: Clinical findings of the patient. (a) A mass lesion of the tongue. The node was round and showed internal heterogeneous echoes; therefore, it was suspected as a metastasis. (d) Computed tomography with contrast. plate_findings.evidence: T2/FLAIR hyperintense signal of the skull lesion in the left frontal bone (caption)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel A is an axial T2/FLAIR MRI showing a calvarial lesion in the left frontal bone. The article title identifies calvarial syphilitic osteomyelitis as a rare manifestation of secondary syphilis, supporting syphilis attribution. [raw subtype: secondary] B: Panel B is an axial DWI/ADC MRI showing the same left frontal calvarial lesion with diffusion restriction. It is part of the same rare secondary syphilis manifestation reported in the article title. [raw subtype: secondary] C: Panel C is an axial DWI/ADC MRI showing the left frontal calvarial lesion with diffusion restriction, part of the reported calvarial syphilitic osteomyelitis. [raw subtype: secondary] D: Panel D is an axial gadolinium-enhanced T1 MRI showing enhancing bone, underlying meninges, and overlying soft tissue at the left frontal calvarial lesion, consistent with the article's syphilitic osteomyelitis diagnosis. [raw subtype: secondary]

in_text_mentions: He consulted a neurosurgeon for his problem, and an MRI brain was ordered to rule out any organic etiologies. A similar but slightly smaller (~1cm) calvarial lesion is also noted in the left parietal bone (Figure 1). Neoplastic and infectious causes were initially considered.

in_text_mentions: A 32-year-old man was referred to the department of dermatology due to an enlarging, painful inflammatory lesion with central breakdown, covered with honey-yellow crusts on the left side of the lower lip (Figure 1). The skin lesions were accompanied by a rise in body temperature to 37.5°C, excessive sweating, and chills. A positive history of herpes labialis at the place of the lesion was noted.
